transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I decided to come in because I just feel like I’m always up and moving around. Even on what is supposed to be a quiet day at home, I’m bouncing from one thing to the next. I'll start looking at my garden club list, then I'll move over to my knitting bag, and then I'm sorting through travel papers... all before I’ve really finished any one of those things. I just can't seem to settle.
Have you had a period of several days when your mood was unusually elevated or very irritable?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my mood is usually pretty steady. I don't get, well, unusually high or angry for days at a time. It's really just the restlessness that bothers me, but my mood itself is fine.
Do you often find it hard to keep your attention on one task, even when you want to?

Yes, I do. It happens quite a bit. I can start out listening fine at a planning meeting, or just be sitting there reading the church bulletin... but after a little while, I'll realize I’ve completely missed half of what was said or printed. I really want to pay attention, but my mind just sort of wanders off without me noticing.
Did these attention and restlessness problems also happen when you were a child?

Yes, they did. Well, even back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was bright, but scattered. I was always losing my papers... and I'd be talking out of turn, or just wiggling around in my seat before I even finished my work. So, yes, it's been like this for a very long time.
